Import machinery · full songs, drum kits & voice memos (local backend)
Needs the local backend running (python backend/crosspollinate_backend.py). Mixes come back as drums.wav + other.wav stems plus a raw transcription; drum-kit zips auto-route recognized pieces into the hub (unrecognized ones get manual “→ armed slot” chips); voice memos auto-apply their transcription to the target track and immediately offer tap-to-beat alignment (Module 4) — accept to collapse into macro-blocks; the 🔗 chip later flips back to the raw transcribed MIDI.

Sample hub · route tracks to external audio (Web Audio buffers)
Synth patches · instant instruments, zero download (a filled hub slot on the same track still wins)
Click a slot to arm it (armed slot also auditions its clip) · drag & drop audio files onto any slot · pitched slots repitch the clip from its root note (↕) or play it untransposed (▪ one-shot) · drum slots are per-piece one-shots · empty slots fall back to the built-in sampled/synth instruments.

Scheduled on the same Web Audio transport as the band (quarter notes, beat-1 accent each bar) — sample-accurate, no setInterval drift. The built-in sound is a synthesized woodblock (bright resonant tick); any dropped sample replaces it for this session, accents play it slightly louder & brighter. Runs whenever the transport plays.

Mixer ✕
Phase 0.5 per client direction (July 2026): Hookpad-style editing first, variation engines layered on top once chords + melody feel right. Melody conformance on chord swap follows the Conformance detents in the palette toolbar (Absolute · Scale · Function · Contour — Feature 1, live): Absolute keeps notes as written, the others conform the melody whenever chords change under it or a source melody lands. Bass and comping are chord-relative and re-render live from the chord lane, including approach-next look-ahead. Piano and drums use sampled acoustic instruments (loaded from the Tone.js sample library on first play; synth fallback if offline). The Sample hub can re-route any track to external audio — local files, Freesound, or Splice-synced/URL buffers — triggered per MIDI note as native Web Audio buffer sources; slots left empty keep the built-in instruments.
